name: Nailed horseshoe
kb: Iron U-shaped shoe nailed to hoof perimeter
note: Nails grip hoof wall without driving into sensitive tissue; the curve distributes load. Works where ground is wet or rocky. Unshod horses slip.

name: Rigid padded horse collar
kb: Padded frame that lets horse pull from shoulders not neck
note: Pressure on chest, not neck blood vessels; a horse can then pull 5 times its own weight. The yoke was strangulation efficiency.

name: Whippletree and swingletree
kb: Hinged bar that pivots to equalize load across multiple animals
note: Each horse pulls equally even if they are different strengths; load distributes by a free pivot. Critical for heavy loads and team hauling.

name: Tandem harness for shafts
kb: Two horses in line sharing draft load via shaft trace system
note: Horses positioned one behind the other; the lead horse sets direction, rear horse pushes. Standard for coaches and heavy wagons.

name: Stirrup with foot loop
kb: Metal loop hung from saddle to support rider foot
note: Allows rider to stand in saddle and apply weight and force; enables mounted combat and faster gaits. Foot placement adds stability.

name: Improved spoked wheel
kb: Radial spokes under tension with metal rim band
note: Tensioned spokes are lighter and stronger than solid wood; the metal rim distributes braking and impact loads. Wheels survive rutted roads.

name: Iron tyre band
kb: Forged iron band shrunk onto wooden wheel rim
note: Iron hardness resists ground wear and stone damage; shrink-fit creates friction grip. Wheel lasts 10 times longer than bare wood on stone.

name: Shrink-fit tyre assembly
kb: Heat iron tyre to expand, slide onto rim, cool to grip
note: Radial pressure from cooling iron clamping the rim; the tyre cannot slip or loosen. Critical process failure if temperature is wrong.

name: Macadam road surface
kb: Layers of small stones compacted into solid binding mass
note: Each stone layer is smaller; compaction by weight and traffic creates shear-lock. Natural road binding without tar; lasts 20 years.

name: Steam road roller
kb: Heavy steam-powered cylinder compacts stone and asphalt
note: Steam piston drives the roller by crank; compaction force is thousands of tonnes. Human-powered rollers took teams of 20 men all day.

name: Tarmacadam: tar-bound stone
kb: Macadam base with hot coal tar binder and top dressing
note: Tar fills voids and binds; prevents water penetration and dust. Lasts 30 years on trunk roads. Less noise and dust than macadam.

name: Reinforced concrete road
kb: Steel-reinforced Portland cement slab laid on prepared base
note: Monolithic slab eliminates rutting and stone rattle; steel prevents cracking under load. Lasts 40 years. Expensive but fast traffic.

name: Cambered road and drainage
kb: Road surface slopes from centre to edges; ditches along sides
note: Water runs off to sides instead of pooling; eliminates mud pits and wheel ruts. Simple geometry; the slope is a few per cent.

name: Kerb and gutter edge
kb: Stone edge strip separates carriageway from sidewalk
note: Defines edge; prevents water and debris escaping onto pavements. Protects pedestrians and controls vehicle paths.

name: Level crossing: road and rail
kb: Road surface raised or lowered to meet rail level at grade
note: Eliminates grade separation cost; risk is collision. Signals, gates and lookouts required. Works only for light traffic or short crossings.

name: Plain journal bearing
kb: Soft metal sleeve around rotating shaft; oil film reduces friction
note: Bronze wears instead of the shaft; replaceable. Oil film is hydrodynamic; bearing runs hot if oil starves. Standard in wooden carts.

name: Roller bearing: cylindrical
kb: Hardened steel cylinders in cage rolling on hardened races
note: Rolling contact reduces friction to 1/10th of sliding; spin is almost frictionless. Cage holds cylinders in place and spacing.

name: Ball bearing: spherical
kb: Hardened steel balls in cage on hardened grooved races
note: Spheres conform to race geometry; friction is 1/100th of plain bearing. Requires tolerance and hardness. Standard in bicycles and motors.

name: Taper roller bearing
kb: Conical rollers in cage on matching conical races
note: Tapers allow combined radial and thrust loading; spreads force over long contact line. Wheel hub and differential support bearings.

name: Grease cup with screw plunger
kb: Cup on bearing with spring plunger; screw forces grease down shaft
note: Periodic manual screw-turn adds grease; spring pressure keeps old grease out. Prevents bearing starvation and water ingress on wagon axles.

name: Oil bath: submerged bearing
kb: Bearing runs submerged in oil; oil clings to parts by capillary action
note: No manual lubrication; oil circulates by splashing. Water and dirt sink to the bottom. Standard on high-speed bicycle hubs and motor bearings.

name: Leaf spring: stacked flat
kb: Curved flat steel leaves stacked and clamped at ends
note: Flat geometry is easy to forge; stacked layers share load and provide damping. Leaf separation under impact; requires periodic re-tensioning.

name: Elliptic spring: single curved
kb: Single curved plate hung from axle; smooth compliance
note: Smoothly distributes bump energy; eliminates stacking friction loss. Used front and rear; lighter and quieter than leaf springs.

name: Coil spring: helical wire
kb: Wire or steel rod wound in helix; compresses under load
note: Uniform spring rate over travel; no friction loss like leaf springs. Compact; fits inside axle tubes. Oscillates without damping.

name: Friction damper: sliding block
kb: Spring-loaded block dragged by spring motion; dissipates energy
note: Slides against fixed surface; friction converts oscillation to heat. Simple and robust; damping is velocity-independent.

name: Hydraulic shock absorber
kb: Piston in oil cylinder; orifice restricts flow and damps motion
note: Oil viscosity and orifice size control damping rate; velocity-dependent. Smooth ride; eliminates spring bounce; separate piston rod for return.

name: Fifth wheel coupling
kb: Articulated hitch between tractor and trailer via rotating disk
note: Low-friction pivot lets trailer turn independently; no stress on kingpin. Enables articulated rigs and half-tracks.

name: Ackermann steering geometry
kb: Front wheels steered so inner wheel turns more than outer
note: Inner wheel scrubs less at full lock; eliminates tire wear in corners and improves cornering stability. All modern steering uses this.

name: Kingpin and steering arm
kb: Vertical pivot pin through steering knuckle with ball bearing
note: Ball bearing lets front wheel turn freely; kingpin takes axial thrust. Caster angle puts turning axis ahead of contact patch for stability.

name: Brake shoe: curved pad
kb: Curved cast iron pad presses on wheel rim or drum by lever
note: Curved form conforms to wheel; friction coefficient is 0.3 to 0.4. Wears smooth; brake fade if overheated. Standard on carts and coaches.

name: Drum brake: shoes in cylinder
kb: Two shoes inside rotating drum; hydraulic or cable pulls them out
note: Enclosed brakes protect from water and mud; self-energizing if shoes are wedged into drum. Fade if overheated; requires cooling time.

name: Disc brake: pad on disk
kb: Brake pads squeeze rotating disk; high friction, excellent cooling
note: Disk cools by convection; no fade even in continuous braking. Linear force; no self-energizing issues. Modern standard.

name: Hydraulic brake line and cylinder
kb: Fluid pressure in hose transmits braking force to four wheels equally
note: Eliminates cable routing and friction; equal pressure on all wheels prevents skew and locks. Requires bleed valves to remove air bubbles.

name: Handbrake: lever and cable
kb: Operator lever pulls cable to engage brake; ratchet holds locked
note: Ratchet lets driver hold vehicle on slope; release is manual. Simple and reliable. Works at parking.

name: Differential: bevel gears
kb: Four-gear spider lets driven wheels turn at different speeds in corners
note: Without this the inside wheel scrubs 15 percent and the axle twists; with it, smooth cornering. Essential for motor vehicles and powered carts.

name: Live axle: powered driving
kb: Axle rotates with wheels; power delivered through shaft inside
note: Propshaft spins inside the axle tube; differential is built into axle casing. Standard on motor vehicles from 1900.

name: Dead axle: non-driven
kb: Axle does not rotate; wheels spin freely on bearings
note: Used for steering and rear trailer axles; no power transmission. Simpler than live axle.

name: Universal joint: Cardan shaft
kb: Double-jointed shaft transmits rotation at angles up to 30 degrees
note: Cruciform spider with needle bearings allows shaft to bend; speed is uniform if using double joints. Essential for connecting engine to axle.

name: Propshaft: transmission shaft
kb: Long shaft with universal joints connects gearbox to differential
note: Must be balanced to avoid vibration; spins 1000 to 6000 rpm. Tube and solid shaft designs; solid is simpler but heavier.

name: Velocipede: pedal-driven wheel
kb: Cranks attached to hub of large wheel; pedals drive directly
note: Direct crank drive means pedal force is proportional to wheel size; large wheel needed for speed. Poor leverage and high pedal rate.

name: Penny-farthing: large wheel
kb: Huge front wheel with pedal cranks, tiny rear wheel
note: Wheel diameter reaches 60 inches; one pedal turn covers 15 feet. Speed is possible; instability and rider height are hazards.

name: Chain drive: roller chain
kb: Rollers on links mesh with sprockets to transmit power
note: Decouples crank size from wheel size; enables small wheel with high speed. Rollers reduce wear on sprockets; chain stretches with use.

name: Safety bicycle: chain-driven
kb: Equal-sized wheels with chain drive to rear wheel
note: Low seat position is stable; handlebar steering is direct. Chain and sprockets allow gear ratios; pedal force is efficient.

name: Freewheel: ratchet hub
kb: Hub spins freely when pedals stop; mechanical ratchet
note: Pawl and ratchet; wheel keeps spinning downhill without pedaling. Eliminates pedal speed constraint; coasting is essential.

name: Derailleur: chain shifter
kb: Pivot arm shifts chain between sprockets; cable controlled
note: Lever or cable shifts chain sideways onto cogs; tension arm maintains chain slack. Requires precise cable routing and spring tuning.

name: Hub gear: internal speeds
kb: Planetary gears inside hub allow multiple speed ratios
note: No derailleur; gears inside sealed hub. Shift under load; no chain slip. More complex than derailleur; self-repairs are difficult.

name: Caliper brake: side-pull
kb: Twin arms pivot at pivot bolt; pads squeeze rim from sides
note: Cable-actuated lever pulls arm; return spring releases. Friction pads require constant replacement. No brake fade on light speeds.

name: Carburettor: fuel atomiser
kb: Moving air through venturi creates vacuum to atomise fuel
note: Bernoulli effect pulls fuel into airstream; float chamber maintains level. Throttle valve controls air flow and mixture ratio.

name: Throttle valve: fuel control
kb: Butterfly valve controls fuel and air intake to engine
note: Cable or linkage to accelerator pedal; spring returns to idle. Mixture enrichment for cold start.

name: Magneto ignition: coil armature
kb: Rotating magnet induces high-voltage pulse in coil at each cylinder
note: Magneto generates its own power from engine rotation; no battery. Timing must advance with rpm for full power.

name: Coil ignition: battery and breaker
kb: Battery powers coil; breaker points open to induce spark at plug
note: Breaker points are mechanical; timing is set by cam lobe. Requires battery maintenance. More reliable than magneto at high speeds.

name: Spark plug: electrode gap
kb: Insulated electrode with air gap in combustion chamber
note: Ceramic insulator withstands 1000 C and high pressure; central electrode is nickel-alloy. Gap requires precise machining and adjustment.

name: Distributor: switching contacts
kb: Rotating contact arm sends voltage to each spark plug in sequence
note: Synchronous with engine rotation; rotor opens and closes circuits. Must handle thousands of switching cycles per minute.

name: Electric starter motor
kb: Battery-powered motor with pinion gear engages flywheel
note: Eliminates hand-crank; starter disengages when engine fires. Bendix drive uses overrunning clutch for safety.

name: Dynamo: rotary power generator
kb: Spinning armature in magnetic field generates voltage to charge battery
note: Engine drives dynamo via belt; output voltage must exceed battery voltage for charging. Regulator disconnects if voltage is too high.

name: Radiator: water cooler
kb: Thin brass tubes and fins cool hot water by exposure to air
note: Fins increase surface area; water flows in at base and out at top by thermosiphon circulation. Cooling must match engine heat output.

name: Water pump: centrifugal
kb: Spinning impeller pushes water through cooling circuit
note: Impeller blades fling water outward; centrifugal force creates pressure head. Thermostat bypass allows fast warm-up.

name: Thermostat: temperature valve
kb: Wax pellet expands with heat; valve restricts bypass to radiator
note: Wax expands at setpoint (around 82 C); opens gradually. Prevents engine overcooling at startup and overheating at full load.

name: Fan belt and pulley drive
kb: V-belt wrapped around pulleys drives cooling fan
note: Belt must be tensioned correctly; slipping causes loss, breakage causes overheating. Replaceable; tension checked periodically.

name: Cone clutch: friction surface
kb: Male and female cones interlock; axial force engages drive
note: Conical geometry increases normal force and torque capacity at shallow angles. Slipping heats both surfaces; requires cooling time.

name: Plate clutch: disk friction
kb: Spring-loaded disk with friction material squeezes between plates
note: Friction material burns if slipped excessively; wear changes pedal feel. Diaphragm spring reduces effort; self-adjusting for wear.

name: Sliding gearbox: mesh shift
kb: Gears slide on shafts to engage different ratios
note: Gears crash if shifted under load; must rev-match or double-clutch. Four to six speeds typical. Crude compared to synchromesh.

name: Synchromesh: synchronizer ring
kb: Friction cone syncs gear speeds before meshing; smooths shift
note: Friction ring accelerates or decelerates gear to match shaft speed; then dog clutch engages. Eliminates grinding and allows fast shifts.

name: Epicyclic gearbox: planetary
kb: Small gears orbit around central sun gear; multiple ratios by holding components
note: Very compact; ratios determined by which element is held fixed. Used in early automatic transmissions and in-wheel motors.

name: Automatic transmission: hydraulic
kb: Hydraulic torque converter shifts gears automatically
note: Torque converter uses hydraulic fluid as transmission medium; pressure regulator shifts gears by engaging clutch packs. Complex and smooth.

name: Fuel pump: mechanical
kb: Cam-operated diaphragm pump lifts fuel from tank to carburettor
note: Diaphragm flexes in and out; check valves direct flow. Operates at engine speed; pressure regulator diverts excess back to tank.

name: Oil pump: pressure lubrication
kb: Geared pump pressurises oil to lubricate engine bearings
note: Pump creates 20 to 60 psi; feeds main gallery and branch lines. Pressure relief valve prevents overpressure. Low pressure warning by float valve.

name: Air filter: intake cleaning
kb: Cloth or paper element traps dust from intake air
note: Prevents sand and dirt from scoring cylinders; must be cleaned frequently. Clogged filter reduces power.

name: Muffler: silencer pipe
kb: Chamber with baffles absorbs exhaust noise
note: Expansion and baffle design attenuate pulsations; silencing is incomplete. Backpressure aids low-end torque.

name: Windscreen wiper: mechanical
kb: Camshaft-driven arm swings wiper blade across glass
note: Vacuum-operated versions use engine intake; direct cam drive is mechanically reliable. Blade must be soft rubber to avoid scratching glass.

name: Headlamp: electric light
kb: Parabolic reflector and incandescent or arc lamp for road lighting
note: Dip and main beam control low and high intensity. Reflector focus determines beam pattern. Carbide lamps use chemical reaction; electric is cleaner.

name: Indicator light: direction signal
kb: Flashing light or arm signals intent to turn
note: Flashing relay opens and closes circuit; amber lens is standard. Arm-based indicators fold down when turn is complete.

name: Omnibus: passenger coach
kb: Large open or enclosed carriage seating 10 to 30 passengers
note: Spring suspension carries multiple passengers smoothly; seats are arranged lengthwise or in rows. Public transport standard from 1820.

name: Tram: horse-drawn
kb: Carriage running on rails pulled by horses
note: Rails reduce rolling resistance and allow heavier load than roads. Wheels flange the rail; tracks are laid in city streets and paved.

name: Tram: steam-powered
kb: Small steam engine on platform drives tram on rails
note: Small steam engine is compact; boiler must be insulated. Track fouling by coal dust is a nuisance. Electric power displaced steam in cities by 1910.

name: Tram: electric powered
kb: Electric motor powered from overhead wires via trolley pole
note: DC motor efficiency and smooth control are superior to steam. Trolley pole reaches overhead conductor; braking recovers energy.

name: Trolleybus: electric bus
kb: Bus-sized vehicle with electric motor powered from overhead wires
note: No rails required; road steering allows flexible routing. Two trolley poles provide redundancy and steady power. Silent and clean.

name: Motor lorry: gasoline truck
kb: Petrol-engined vehicle for cargo transport
note: Cab over engine or conventional layout; payload 2 to 5 tonnes. Four-speed gearbox and live axle. Air brake lines for trailer.

name: Articulated trailer: semi-trailer
kb: Unpowered trailer coupled with fifth wheel to powered tractor
note: Trailer carries 10 to 20 tonnes; fifth wheel distribution allows tractor to navigate tight corners. Payload efficiency gains 50 percent.

name: Tractor: agricultural motorvehicle
kb: Low-speed high-torque motor with power takeoff for implements
note: Three-point hitch connects implements; PTO shaft drives threshers, pumps, balers. Wide tyres and low centre-of-gravity for soft ground.

name: Caterpillar track: endless belt
kb: Linked steel shoes on driving sprockets distribute load over wide area
note: Tracks climb steep slopes and cross soft ground; mud does not cling to shoes. Higher traction than wheels. Used on tanks and heavy dozers.

name: Half-track vehicle
kb: Tracks at rear, steered wheels at front
note: Front wheels steer; tracks handle traction. Lower cost than full track; faster on roads. Used in WW2 for soft-ground transport.

name: Motorcycle: two-wheeled motor
kb: Single-cylinder engine in bicycle frame with motorcycle tyres
note: Three to 8 horsepower typical; motorcycle tyres must have grip. Lightweight and manoeuvrable; no weather protection. Sidecar extends payload.

name: Snow plough: powered blade
kb: V-shaped blade mounted on truck clears snow from road surface
note: Hydraulic lift raises or lowers blade; angling lifts pushes snow to side. Rock and gravel damage blades; steel edge replaceable.

name: Pneumatic tyre: air-filled
kb: Rubber envelope filled with air; sidewalls flex to absorb bumps
note: Air spring is light and effective; pinch-flats require inner tube. Rotation must be balanced or vibration results. Puncture repair by patching.

name: Inner tube: rubber bladder
kb: Separate air-holding tube inside tyre; prevents pinch-flats
note: Valve stem allows inflation and deflation; seals against tyre bead. Pinch-flats occur when rim hits bump with low pressure.

name: Tyre bead: rim seat
kb: Reinforced edge of tyre seats onto wheel rim
note: Wire or cord-reinforced ring prevents tyre slipping on rim under load. Bead tension must match rim diameter for safe seating.

name: Tyre tread pattern
kb: Grooves carved into tyre surface channel water away from contact patch
note: Grooves remove water from contact patch and improve grip; sipes add biting edges at low temperatures. Tread wear is main tyre life limit.

name: Solid rubber tyre
kb: Thick rubber wheel without air; hard and durable
note: Does not puncture; very heavy and hard. Poor ride quality; vibration is severe. Bounce is minimal. Used on trolleys and industrial wheels.

name: DC electric motor
kb: Rotating coil in permanent magnet field powered by DC current
note: Commutator and brushes switch current direction as coil rotates; torque is continuous. Brushes require maintenance; arcing causes wear.
